name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: The original AI pair programmer, now baked directly into GitHub and every major IDE.
tldr: GitHub Copilot is an AI coding assistant available as a plugin/extension for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, Eclipse, and Xcode, plus a CLI and GitHub.com integration.
Best for developers already living inside the GitHub ecosystem who want autocomplete, chat, code review, and agentic workflows without switching editors.

Moved to usage-based/token billing in 2026, where each paid plan bundles a monthly pool of AI credits that get consumed by chat, agent mode, code review, and the CLI, while basic code completions stay unmetered.
Offers model choice (GPT, Claude, Gemini variants) across its Pro, Pro+, and Max tiers, with Business/Enterprise tiers adding org-wide policy controls and audit logs.
Faces recurring community criticism over how aggressively Copilot prompts are surfaced across GitHub's UI and over premium-request limits pushing users toward pricier tiers.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 2,000 completions/month, access to Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5 mini, Copilot CLI, no credit card required

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Unlimited code completions, $15/mo bundled AI credits, cloud agent access, code review

plans.name: Pro+
plans.notes: $70/mo bundled AI credits, premium models including Opus, audit logs

plans.name: Max
plans.notes: $200/mo bundled AI credits, priority access to new models, built for high-volume agent workflows

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: Org-wide policy management and centralized billing

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud (adds ~$21/user/mo); custom models, codebase indexing, enhanced GitHub.com integration

pros: Works natively across nearly every major editor and IDE, not just one
Free tier is genuinely usable (2,000 completions/month) before requiring payment
Tight integration with GitHub itself for code review, pull requests, and Actions
Long track record and broad enterprise adoption makes procurement/security review easier for large orgs
cons: Recent shift to usage-based/token billing has confused users about what a given plan actually includes
Premium request limits on lower tiers push heavy users toward the pricier Pro+/Max plans
Some developers find Copilot prompts and nudges surfaced too aggressively throughout GitHub's and VS Code's UI
Suggestions can be inaccurate or generic for unusual codebases, requiring careful review before accepting

sentiment.quote: Cursor is pretty solid, especially for quick completions, but Copilot just feels more polished and reliable.

Although Microsoft's been forcing the Copilot 'asks' into more and more places in the interface for a while, sometime this year they hit an inflection point where mass numbers of people don't feel like ignoring it anymore, where before they could shrug and ignore it or find the off switch.
Six months ago, I was skeptical about AI coding tools... I was wrong. Dead wrong.

bestFor: Teams already standardized on GitHub for source control and CI/CD
Developers who want AI assistance without leaving their existing IDE
Enterprises that need org-wide policy controls, audit logs, and procurement-friendly vendor history
Individuals who want a capable free tier before committing to a paid plan
hotTake: Copilot's 2026 move to token-based billing means the $10 sticker price is just the entry fee — Pro+ users get a $70 credit pool that can evaporate fast under agent workflows.
